analysis:
Market regime: SPY is in a moderate uptrend (+0.5% vs SMA50, slope +1.21%), which is constructive but not euphoric. No reason to panic-cash, but no reason to chase either.

PORTFOLIO REVIEW — honest assessment required:
The track record is deeply alarming: 10% win rate, avg loss -5.37%, avg win +2.06%, profit factor 0.03x, Sortino -12.81. This is materially underperforming a passive SPY hold. Five consecutive stop-outs reinforce that entries have been poorly timed and/or position sizing has absorbed losses that compound into real damage. The mandate here is capital preservation first.

Existing positions:
- NVDA (+2.86%): Only winner. Still on screened list with extraordinary fundamentals (ROE 117%, op margin 66%, EPS revision +22.6%). Hold; consider tightening stop to protect the gain.
- AMP (-1.14%): Not appearing in this cycle's screened candidates — may be drifting on quality metrics. Loss is modest but the prior AMP trade was also stopped out (-3.81%). Watch closely; if price falls through SMA50 decisively, consider exiting.
- MCO (-0.55%): Essentially flat, thesis (duopoly ratings business) intact. Not in screened list this cycle — hold but monitor.
- BR (-3.24%): Most concerning. Not in screened list, underwater, and the trend of losses on prior stops is a warning. If stop level is reached, respect it.

New trades: Given 63% deployment and the catastrophic win rate, I am proposing only ONE new position — TEL — which offers the cleanest Stage 1-to-2 basing setup on the screened list: 21% of 52w range, SMA50 essentially flat (-0.4%), positive SMA50 slope, quality fundamentals at a fair price (fwd P/E 15.9, PEG 0.88). All other high-scoring candidates are either extended (ANET 88%, CVX 89%, APA 90%, ZBRA 80%+), have imminent earnings risk (FDS 9d, ACN 10d), show declining EPS revisions (UHS -4.6%, PSKY -4.7%, MOS -16.5%), or are extended from SMA50 (CRM +15.2%, PLTR +12.2%). Cash preservation is the right call for the remainder of the headroom.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $205.00 or on a small intraday pullback to the $202-205 zone; do not chase above $208. The stock is basing tightly around SMA50 — a day of mild weakness is a better entry than market-order urgency.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: TE Connectivity is a high-quality industrial connector and sensor business with durable competitive advantages in harsh-environment electronics. Fwd P/E 15.9, PEG 0.88, ROE 23.3%, operating margin 20.8%, and $2.3B FCF give a clear margin of safety. Revenue growth of 13.8% and EPS revisions +2.3% confirm the business is growing, not deteriorating. The stock trades at a material discount to its 52w high ($246), suggesting it was sold off on macro/sector rotation rather than fundamental deterioration. TECHNICAL: At 21% of its 52w range, TEL sits in the lower half where risk/reward is best. Price is -0.4% from SMA50 with SMA50 slope barely positive (+0.2%) — the classic Weinstein Stage 1 basing-to-Stage 2 transition. The stock has not confirmed a downtrend and is consolidating above recent support near $194. ATR-based stop at $196 gives 4.4% downside risk with ~12% upside to fair-value recovery, yielding RR >2.7x. Earnings 37 days out provide adequate runway before binary event risk.
trades.exit_plan: Hard stop at $196. Time stop: if stock fails to make progress toward SMA200 within 8 weeks, reassess and exit even without stop being hit. Thesis-break: exit on any earnings miss paired with downward guidance revision. Trail stop up by 1x ATR for every 5% gain above entry. Do not hold through earnings if the stock has not shown meaningful progress — consider reducing to half size before the Oct 28 print if position is flat or negative.
